messages.subject: range definition of parameters prior
parts:
Dear Experts,
    I was trying to use stan to estimate the parameters of Fehr-Schmidt Inequality Model. Below are details of this model:
U(s,o) = s - alpha*max{o-s,0}-beta*max{s-o,0} 
Note: s refers to "self payoff"，o refers to "other payoff"; aplha refers to people's aversion to disadvantageous inequality (i.e. I don't like that I got less money than the other person);  beta refers to people's aversion to advantageous inequality (i.e. I don't like that I got more money than the other person).

   This model assumes that people in general are more aversive to disadvantageous than advantageous inequality. Thus it has the following range for alpha and beta:
   0<alpha, 0<beta<min(alpha,1)
   Here are my way to express the above constraints in stan code:
parameters {
  real <lower=0> alpha; //alpha: disadvantageous inequality aversion parameter
  real <lower=0> beta; //beta: advantageous inequality aversion parameter
}

model { 
  //subject's priors: beta
  //range: 0 < beta < min(alpha,1)
  beta ~ beta(0.5,1);
  //subject's priors: alpha 
  //range: 0 < alpha
  alpha ~ beta(0.5+beta,1);
...

    I don't think it is correct. But I have no idea that how I should do this. Would any of you can help me with that?
    I'm looking forward to your reply :-) Thanks a lot for your help. 

Best,
Yang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] range definition of parameters prior
parts: You can code it up just how you wrote it:

You can code that up directly, but it's an odd constraint (not
differentiable at alpha = 1 and flat with alpha > 1):

parameters {
real<lower = 0> alpha;
real<lower = 0, upper = min(alpha, 1)> beta;

So it might not work well with HMC if the value of alpha is near 1
and it has to cross over the boundary alpha = 1.

But I would suggest not trying to put a hard constraint on
the parameters, but rather something softer and then making sure
the data bears out your prior.

- Bob
